POOLED METRIC · ALL FOUR DEPARTMENTS

Spot premium dollars

—

Needs comparable cost inputs

Extra cost compared with a contract benchmark for the same spot loads. Aim to reduce it while protecting delivery.

Total spot freight cost—
Spot share of freight cost—

Premium = actual spot cost − comparable contracted cost. A negative result means spot was cheaper than the benchmark. Total spot cost answers how much spend came from spot freight.

PRODUCTION PLANNING

Early-release rate

—

Needs release counts

Percentage of loads released to logistics at least 48 hours before scheduled pickup. Aim to increase it so logistics has more time to book carriers.

Enter total loads, early loads and missing-timestamp loads.

Rate = loads released ≥48 hours early ÷ all loads due for pickup in the period. Use one record per load. Missing release timestamps stay in the denominator and do not count as early.

Update metric inputs

Use the same evaluation period and flows below. These manually entered metrics are independent of the historical freight filters. The case workbook does not provide matched spot invoices or release timestamps.

Pooled cost inputs

Use comparable all-in costs, including fuel and accessorials. A benchmark comparison does not establish that contract capacity was available. Rate averages and the workbook’s Overspend field are not substituted for actual spot costs.

Production planning inputs

Count early when release time ≤ scheduled pickup time − 48 hours. Use timestamps with the same time basis, the original scheduled pickup time, and a consistent rule for cancellations. The dashboard calculates the rate from these entered counts.

ONE RESULT · FOUR DEPARTMENTS

Save together. Share the gain.

Long-term forecasting, short-term forecasting, production planning and logistics share one pool based on net freight savings. Protect delivery while reducing costly emergency freight.

Needs cost inputs
USER-ENTERED PROPOSAL

Measure the savings fairly

Use the same period and shipment scope for all inputs. Adjust the baseline for volume, lane mix, fuel and market changes. Include contract and spot freight, transfers, accessorials and service recovery costs.

Extra costs include implementation or inventory costs outside the actual freight figure. Count each cost once. Enter delivery as a percentage, such as 95 for 95%. These inputs are independent of Performance filters.

Proposed pool

max(0, adjusted baseline − actual cost − extra costs) × gainshare rate

    DATA COVERAGE

    What this dashboard can establish

    Available

    Monthly OTD and recorded freight mix by month, lane, load group, and carrier.

    Not supplied

    Daily tender timestamps, carrier commitments or refusals, order IDs, order changes, shipment errors, material receipts, inventory shortages, and production-change reasons.

    Unconfirmed definitions

    PTA%, FMI, and the operational volume unit. PTA% and FMI are excluded from calculations.

    CALCULATION NOTES

    Numbers teams can explain

    Spot share

    SUM(SM Volume) / SUM(Total Volume)

    Volume-weighted, never an average of row percentages. Contract + spot volume reconciles to total volume in every source detail record.

    On-time delivery

    Mean of supplied monthly OTD percentages

    The workbook supplies monthly percentages without shipment denominators. KPI cards show an unweighted monthly mean, not a shipment-weighted period rate. These measures cannot be filtered to lanes or carriers.

    Average base freight rate

    SUM(Avg Base × Total Volume) / SUM(covered volume)

    Only records with numeric Avg Base (USD) enter the average. Coverage is shown. Changes can reflect a different mix of routes or carriers, not just price changes.

    Comparison periods

    Prior year, same available selected months

    2026 stops in July. Prior-year comparisons use the same months available for the selected year. With all years selected, year-over-year comparisons are disabled.

    Case narrative versus workbook totals

    The case cites 15–20% spot reliance. The original case workbook’s Detail aggregate for January–July 2026 is 7.9% across all load groups. Their period, scope, and basis are not reconciled, so those figures should not be treated as interchangeable.

    Rates, savings, and causes

    Avg Base and Avg Primary Rate are freight fields. They do not establish aluminum purchase costs. The workbook’s Overspend field is not a verified savings opportunity. Spot use does not itself establish a late delivery or raw-material shortage.
